chunk_findings.detail: `_findings_by_bucket` iterates `ctx.facts.findings` without restricting to `REVIEW_GATES`, but `build` uses its result for `findings`, `findings_per_run`, `confirmed`, `refuted`, and `confirmed_rate` in a review-run table. If an item has one review run and one confirmed finding on a non-review gate (for example `gate="test"`), the bucket row reports `findings_per_run=1.0` and `confirmed_rate=100%` while `runs_with_finding=0%`, even though no review finding exists. The review economics table should count only review-gate findings, or at least findings tied to the review gates used for runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:_findings_by_bucket

chunk_findings.detail: `_runs_by_bucket` filters review outcomes with `ctx.in_scope(o.item, o.at)`, but both `with_finding` and `_findings_by_bucket` include every finding regardless of scope. Given a scoped query that excludes item B’s outcomes, B’s findings are still bucketed by B’s size and counted against in-scope item A’s review runs in the same bucket, inflating `findings_per_run`, `confirmed`, `refuted`, and `confirmed_rate`; if B is the only item in a bucket, `confirmed_rate` can make `has_figures()` true and cause the command to report data despite zero in-scope review runs. Findings must be scope-filtered the same way as runs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:_runs_by_bucket

chunk_findings.detail: `build()` computes `lock_wait` for every bucket, but `text()` never prints it and `has_figures()` ignores it. Once `waited_s` is recorded, a log whose only usable review evidence is lock-wait data (elapsed values missing and findings below `min_samples`) yields `has_figures() == False`, so `ddflow metrics batch` exits with “not enough data”, and the human output has no lock-wait column even though the intent and module docstring say the command includes the lock wait. The computed `lock_wait` should be rendered and counted as a figure, with low-sample states named in `unavailable`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:text

chunk_findings.detail: `_findings_by_bucket` buckets every finding in `ctx.facts.findings`, but `findings_per_run` and the row’s `findings` are divided by in-scope review runs. Given an item with one in-scope review run and one finding from a non-review gate (or outside the metrics context’s time scope), `_runs_by_bucket` counts one review run while `_findings_by_bucket` still counts that finding. The resulting row reports `findings: 1`, `findings_per_run: 1`, and `confirmed`/`refuted` based on the non-review finding, even though the table is defined over review-gate runs. The run loop filters on `REVIEW_GATES` and `ctx.in_scope(...)`; the finding loop does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:_findings_by_bucket

chunk_findings.detail: The human output never renders `lock_wait`, although `build` computes it and the stated intent is to include the review gate-lock wait in `ddflow metrics batch`. Given a log where review outcomes have `waited_s` values, `build` populates `lock_wait` in the bucket row, but `text` prints only items, runs, elapsed p50, findings/run, runs-with-finding, and confirmed rate. The CLI/MCP human form therefore cannot show the requested lock-wait measurement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:text

chunk_findings.detail: `has_figures` ignores `lock_wait`. Given review runs that recorded `waited_s` but no usable `elapsed_s`, no findings, and no confirmed/refuted findings, `build` produces a non-None `lock_wait` statistic, but `has_figures` checks only `elapsed.p50_s`, `findings_per_run`, `runs_with_finding`, and `confirmed_rate`. It returns false, causing the command to report “not enough data” and discard the only available lock-wait figure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:has_figures

chunk_findings.detail: `build` returns only `group_by`, `buckets`, and `unavailable`. It does not produce the merge-window overlap table or the batch-eligible share required by the change intent. For any input log, the batch service’s returned data lacks those tables, so `ddflow metrics batch` cannot reproduce the stated research tables from the log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: `OV.build(ctx, size)` is called without the batch function's `minimum` sample threshold. The same function already uses `minimum` to decide whether elapsed figures are unavailable (`unavailable[f"elapsed:{r['bucket']}"] = ... need {minimum}`), so the overlap table must honor the same requested threshold. For example, if `batch(ctx, minimum=5)` is called on a log that has only 4 time-overlapping, path-disjoint merge-window pairs, the elapsed figures are correctly marked unavailable, but the overlap table is still built with `OV.build`'s default threshold and rendered instead of being `None`/omitted as the min-sample rule and the added `test_overlap_is_none_not_zero_below_min_samples` require. The overlap builder needs `minimum` passed or otherwise propagated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/batch.py:141

chunk_findings.detail: `small` treats a measured size of `0` as unknown because `size.get(i)` is falsy. For example, if item A has size `0`, item B has size `100`, their leases overlap, and their globs are disjoint, A is omitted from `small`; the pair is then not marked batch-eligible, so `build` returns `eligible_items=0` and an eligible share of 0 even though both items are within `ELIGIBLE_MAX_LINES`. The check should distinguish missing/`None` size from zero, e.g. `i in size and size[i] is not None and size[i] <= ELIGIBLE_MAX_LINES`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/overlap.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: The `MAX_PAIRS` limit is checked after `pairs` has already been incremented, so the pair that exceeds the cap is still counted in `pairs_overlapping`. With `MAX_PAIRS = 200_000` and 200,001 time-overlapping pairs, `build` returns `pairs_overlapping=200001` and `truncated=True`, while `text` says “stopped at 200000 pairs”. The limit check should occur before incrementing, or use `>= MAX_PAIRS`, so the reported count matches the stated cap.

chunk_findings.detail: `small` excludes items whose changed-line count is exactly `0` because `size.get(i)` is falsy for `0`. A known size of zero lines is within `ELIGIBLE_MAX_LINES`, but the comprehension drops it. For example, with two in-scope items whose lease windows overlap and whose globs are disjoint, and `size = {"a": 0, "b": 0}` with `min_samples <= 2`, the expected batch-eligible share is 1.0; `small` is empty, `eligible` remains empty, and `eligible_share` becomes `0.0`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/overlap.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: An item with one lease that has no globs and another lease that does have globs is still treated as having known globs. `_windows` unions `lease.globs`, so an empty `lease.globs` leaves no trace; `_disjoint` only returns false when the union is empty. Given item `a` with two in-scope closed leases, first `globs=()` and second `globs=("src/a.py",)`, and item `b` with `globs=("src/b.py",)`, the code gives `a` the globs `("src/a.py",)`, calls `_disjoint` true, and can mark it batch-eligible. The docstring says an item whose lease named no glob is never called disjoint, so this input violates the stated unknown-is-not-disjoint rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/overlap.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: `for b in order[n + 1:]` copies the remaining ordered list on every outer iteration, making `build` allocate O(n^2) list elements even when `MAX_PAIRS` prevents many pairs from being examined. For a log with 100,000 in-scope items whose lease windows are sorted and non-overlapping, the inner loop breaks after the first `b` for each `a`, so fewer than `MAX_PAIRS` overlapping pairs are processed, but the slices allocate roughly 5 billion list elements total and can stall or exhaust memory. This defeats the stated purpose of `MAX_PAIRS` as a guard against huge logs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/overlap.py:63

evidence.note: ddflow dupes BG-measure: only sibling BG tasks (different scopes, 0.58-0.68); the follow-up I filed that duplicated the overlap work was retitled to the code/test/doc split that is still missing

data.reason: roborev not installed on this host; ruff check and ruff format --check clean on the changed files, the file-size/complexity architecture guards pass (same 3 baseline failures as main)

evidence.note: roborev jobs 4750 and 4751 on the branch range: first run 1 medium (overlap not counted as data) and 1 low (unreachable held-lease branch), both fixed with a test; second run 4 low: 2 fixed in 51ee03bc3 (truncated share None, one finding definition), 2 accepted (constant replaced by BG-policy knob; overlap items as a figure is the fix for the earlier medium). ruff check/format clean.

bug hunt by reading the diff and the reviewers' rounds: scope/gate filter, lock wait render, zero-size handling (zero is unknown by design), glob-less lease, pair cap off-by-one and slice copies, truncation share: each real one fixed with a test that failed first; 15 tests in tests/test_metrics_batch_baseline.py

baseline.isolation: fresh detached worktree of the base; the project's own command ran in it, so an editable install of the branch or git-ignored fixtures can still mislead it

ci_scope.why: 15 test file(s) its change reaches, 27 always-run guard file(s); the selected tests failed; the always-run guards failed
